[[Santa Clara, California]] | champions = [[2018 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] | heisman = [[Kyler Murray]], QB, [[2018 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Oklahoma]] | ap_poll = [[2018 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]]{{cite web|url=https://collegefootball.ap.org/poll|title=The AP Top 25 Poll|publisher=The Associated Press}} | coaches_poll = [[2018 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]]{{cite web|url=http://sportspolls.usatoday.com/ncaa/football/polls/coaches-poll/2018/16|title=Amway Coaches Poll|publisher=USA Today}} }} The '''2018 NCAA Division I FBS football season''' was the 149th season of college football in the United States organized by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) at its highest level of competition, the Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS). The regular season began on August 25, 2018, and ended on December 8, 2018. The postseason began on December 15, and aside from any all-star games that were scheduled, concluded on January 7, 2019, with the [[2019 College Football Playoff National Championship]] at [[Levi's Stadium]] in [[Santa Clara, California|Santa Clara]], [[California]]. The [[2018 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson Tigers]] won the title game over the [[2018 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama Crimson Tide]], the school's third national title and second in three years, and also becoming the first team since the [[1897 Penn Quakers football team|1897 Penn Quakers]] to have a perfect 15-0 season. ==Rule changes== ===Game rules=== The following rule changes were approved by the NCAA Playing Rules Oversight Panel for the 2018 season:{{cite news|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/change-footballs-kickoff-rule-recommended|title=Changes to football's kickoff rule recommended|author=ncaa.org |work=ncaa.org |date=March 2, 2018|access-date=March 3, 2018}} * Allow players to fair catch the ball inside the 25 yard line on a kickoff and be awarded a touchback, placing the ball at the 25 yard line. * Offensive players cannot block below the waist more than five yards past the line of scrimmage and, with the exception of interior linemen, all blocks below the waist must be from the front. * The play clock will be set to 40 seconds between a touchdown and the PAT or two-point conversion and after a kickoff. * Mirroring the NFL rule adopted in the [[2010 NFL season|2010 season]], a 10-second runoff will be applied within the final minute of each half if a replay review overturns the call on the field, and the correct ruling would not have stopped the game clock. As with any other 10 second runoff, teams can take a time out (if available) to avoid the runoff. * Extending the "no leaping" rule on PATs and field goals adopted in the [[2017 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2017 season]] to include the "shield" on a punt. * Allowing penalties incurred on successful field goals to be enforced on the ensuing kickoff, which matches the rule for successful extra point attempts. * Continuing the experiment of a collaborative instant replay decision making model not confined to the press box. ===Eligibility rules=== Major changes to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] rules in Division I football (both FBS and FCS) took effect from this season forward after having been approved by the NCAA Division I Council on June 13, 2018. Players can now participate in as many as four games in a season while still retaining redshirt status. This new rule does not apply to players who enroll at a school midyear and participate in postseason competition taking place during or before their first academic term at that school.{{cite press release|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/di-football-offer-more-participation-opportunities |title=DI football to offer more participation opportunities |publisher=NCAA |date=June 13, 2018 |access-date=July 27, 2018}} ==Conference realignment== ===Membership changes=== {| class="wikitable sortable" !School !Former conference !New conference |- | [[Idaho Vandals football|Idaho Vandals]] | [[Sun Belt Conference|Sun Belt]] | [[Big Sky Conference|Big Sky (FCS)]] |- | [[New Mexico State Aggies football|New Mexico State Aggies]] | Sun Belt | [[NCAA Division I FBS independent schools|FBS independent]] |- | [[Liberty Flames football|Liberty Flames]] | [[Big South Conference|Big South (FCS)]] | FBS independent |} New Mexico State left the [[Sun Belt Conference]] following the 2017 season and will compete as an FBS independent. Idaho also left the Sun Belt, dropping its football program from the FBS to [[Football Championship Subdivision|FCS]] level, where it will compete in the [[Big Sky Conference]]. [[Liberty Flames football|Liberty]] began a two-year transition from FCS in [[2017 Liberty Flames football team|2017]]. The Flames will be counted as an FBS independent for scheduling purposes in 2018, but will not be fully bowl-eligible until the 2019 season. However, they may participate in a bowl in 2018 if they have at least six eligible wins and there are not enough bowl-eligible teams to fill all the spots. ==Other headlines== * July 13 – Following reports that [[Papa John's Pizza]] founder [[John Schnatter]] had said the [[nigger|"n-word"]] in an internal conference call, which led to his resignation both as company chairman and member of the [[University of Louisville]] board of trustees, university president [[Neeli Bendapudi]] announced that the company's name would be removed from the [[L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium|Cardinal Stadium]] name effective immediately.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/24088014/university-louisville-drops-papa-john-name-stadium |title=Louisville's football stadium now known as Cardinal Stadium |first=Andrea |last=Adelson |website=ESPN.com |date=July 13, 2018 |access-date=July 13, 2018}} * August 1 – [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] administrators placed head coach [[Urban Meyer]] on paid administrative leave while the school announced it was launching an investigation into claims that Meyer knew of former assistant coach Zach Smith's involvement in a 2015 domestic violence incident against his ex-wife Courtney Smith. Zach Smith had been fired on July 23 after the allegations were made public.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24258253/ohio-state-buckeyes-places-urban-meyer-administrative-leave |title=Ohio State puts Urban Meyer on administrative leave |website=ESPN.com |date=August 1, 2018 |access-date=August 1, 2018}} ** August 22 – Following the investigation, Ohio State announced that Meyer would be suspended for the first three games of the 2018 season. In addition, athletic director [[Gene Smith (athletic director)|Gene Smith]] was suspended from August 31 to September 16.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24449427/ohio-state-suspends-coach-urban-meyer-ad-gene-smith|title=Ohio State suspends coach Urban Meyer, AD Gene Smith|last=Murphy|first=Dan|date=August 23, 2018|access-date=August 28, 2018|website=ESPN.com}} * August 11 – [[University of Maryland, College Park|Maryland]] placed head coach [[D. J. Durkin]] on paid administrative leave during the school's investigation into the death of player [[Jordan McNair]] from heatstroke following an offseason practice, in addition to allegations of abuse and disparagement by coaches within the program. This announcement came the day after the school had placed two trainers and the team's strength coach on administrative leave.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24351245/maryland-football-coach-dj-durkin-put-leave-amid-reports-toxic-culture |title=Maryland head coach DJ Durkin placed on administrative leave |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |website=ESPN.com |date=August 1, 2018 |access-date=August 1, 2018}} ** August 14 – Maryland president [[Wallace Loh]] announced that the school "accepts legal and moral responsibility for the mistakes" that led to McNair's death. The university also parted ways with Rick Court, the strength coach widely blamed for establishing the alleged culture of abuse revealed in recent news reports. Court had resigned the previous day, and reached a financial settlement with the university shortly before Loh made his announcement.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24374654/maryland-terrapins-accept-responsibility-mistakes-made-death-jordan-mcnair |title=Maryland accepts responsibility in death of Jordan McNair, parts with Rick Court |first=Heather |last=Dinich |website=ESPN.com |date=August 14, 2018 |access-date=August 14, 2018}} ** October 31 – A day after Durkin was reinstated as head coach after the completion of the school's probe, resulting in widespread outrage among state politicians, students, faculty, and members of McNair's family, Loh fired Durkin. [[Matt Canada]], who had been named the interim head coach following Durkin's original suspension, continued in that role for the remainder of the season.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/25137549/maryland-terrapins-football-coach-dj-durkin-fired-one-day-reinstatement |title=Maryland fires football coach DJ Durkin day after his reinstatement |website=ESPN.com |date=October 31, 2018 |access-date=October 31, 2018}} * September 8 – Two of the longest futility streaks of their types in FBS history ended: ** First, in an afternoon game in [[Kelly/Shorts Stadium|Mount Pleasant, Michigan]], [[2018 Kansas Jayhawks football team|Kansas]] defeated [[2018 Central Michigan Chippewas football team|Central Michigan]] 31–7, ending the longest road losing streak in FBS history at 46 games. The only longer such streak in college football history was the 48-game streak of FCS [[Idaho State Bengals football|Idaho State]], which ended in [[2014 Idaho State Bengals football team|2014]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401013049 |title=Kansas routs Central Michigan, snaps 46-game road skid |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=September 8, 2018 |access-date=September 9, 2018}} ** In a night game, [[2018 Kentucky Wildcats football team|Kentucky]] defeated [[2018 Florida Gators football team|Florida]] 27–16 for the Wildcats' first win over the Gators since [[1986 Kentucky Wildcats football team|1986]] and ending the longest current losing streak in an uninterrupted series at 31 games. This streak was the fourth-longest of its type in NCAA history. This also marked Kentucky's first win in [[Ben Hill Griffin Stadium|Gainesville]] since [[1979 Kentucky Wildcats football team|1979]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401012263 |title=Kentucky stuns No. 25 Florida; first win over Gators since '86 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=September 8, 2018 |access-date=September 9, 2018}} * October 28 – Following a weekend in which eight teams ranked in the [[AP Poll]] lost to unranked teams—the most since that poll expanded to a Top 25 format in [[1989 NCAA Division I-A football season|1989]]—seven new teams entered the poll for Week 10, the most in the Top 25 era.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/25107759/record-changes-top-25-11-ranked-losses |title=Syracuse, Virginia move into Top 25 in big shake-up |agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |date=October 28, 2018 |access-date=October 28, 2018}} * November 24 ** The [[2018 LSU vs. Texas A&M football game|LSU–Texas A&M game]], played at [[Kyle Field]] in [[College Station, Texas]], went to seven overtimes and lasted nearly five hours, tying the NCAA record for longest football game with four others.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2018/11/25/it-took-seven-overtimes-texas-am-beat-lsu-craziest-college-football-game-year/ |title=It took seven overtimes for Texas A&M to beat LSU in the craziest college football game of the year |date=November 25, 2018 |first=Cindy |last=Boren |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=November 25, 2018}} The Aggies slipped past the Tigers 74–72. At the time, the 146 combined points were the second most in college football history since the NCAA started keeping records in 1937, behind the 161 points scored in a 2008 [[NCAA Division II]] game between [[Abilene Christian Wildcats football|Abilene Christian]] and [[West Texas A&M Buffaloes football|West Texas A&M]] of the [[Lone Star Conference]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/25370018/texas-tops-lsu-74-72-seventh-over |title=Aggies top LSU in 7 OTs in highest-scoring game in FBS history |date=November 25, 2018 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN News Services |access-date=November 25, 2018}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/124864/100-years-ago-georgia-techs-222-0-victory |title=100 years ago: Georgia Tech's 222-0 victory |date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[ESPN]] |first=Michael |last=Freer |publisher=ESPN Stats & Information |access-date=November 25, 2018}} ** In addition, two notable postseason results were for all intents and purposes confirmed: *** [[2018 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State's]] loss to rival [[2018 Florida Gators football team|Florida]] 41–14 ended the program's Division I FBS-leading streak of 36 consecutive appearances in a postseason bowl game, as the team finished 5–7, and failed to reach bowl eligibility.{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2018/10/30/18040614/ncaa-consecutive-bowl-streak-record-florida-state-florida |title=Florida ends FSU's nation-leading bowl streak, and now VT can *actually* have the longest |website=SBNation.com |agency=Vox Media |date=November 24, 2018 |access-date=November 27, 2018}} *** [[2018 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame's]] win over rival [[2018 USC Trojans football team|USC]] 24-17 resulted in the Fighting Irish completing their first undefeated regular season since [[2012 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|2012]]. The previous record of eight had been accomplished by six teams, most recently by [[2017 LSU Tigers football team|LSU in 2017]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401032056 |title=Georgia Southern tops Eastern Michigan 23-21 on Bass' FG |agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |date=December 15, 2018 |access-date=December 16, 2018}} * December 20 – In a more ignominious milestone, [[2018 South Florida Bulls football team|South Florida]] ended its season in the [[2018 Gasparilla Bowl|Gasparilla Bowl]] with a 38–20 loss to [[2018 Marshall Thundering Herd football team|Marshall]], becoming the first FBS team ever to finish a season 7–6 after a 7–0 start.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/25541689/the-most-important-takeaway-bowl-game |title=The most important takeaway for each college bowl game |work=ESPN.com |access-date=December 23, 2018}} * December 22 – [[2018 Army Black Knights football team|Army]] tied two records for all Division I bowl games in its 70–14 blowout of [[2018 Houston Cougars football team|Houston]] in the [[2018 Armed Forces Bowl|Armed Forces Bowl]]. The 70 points equaled [[2011 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia's]] output against [[2011 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] in the [[2012 Orange Bowl]] (70–33), and the victory margin equaled that of [[2007 Tulsa Golden Hurricane football team|Tulsa]] against [[2007 Bowling Green Falcons football team|Bowling Green]] in the [[2008 GMAC Bowl]] (63–7). It was also the first time since [[1955 Army Cadets football team|1955]] that the Black Knights had scored 70 points in a game, and capped off the team's first-ever 11-win season.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401032064 |title=Army caps 11-win season with record-tying blowout vs. Houston |website=ESPN.com |date=December 22, 2018 |access-date=December 23, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2018/12/22/18153240/army-houston-final-score-results-2018 |title=Holy hell, look at Army's record-setting annihilation of Houston |first=Alex |last=Kirshner |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |date=December 22, 2018 |access-date=December 23, 2018}} * December 27 – In its 63–14 blowout of [[2018 Purdue Boilermakers football team|Purdue]] in the [[2018 Music City Bowl|Music City Bowl]], [[2018 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]] led 56–7 at halftime, setting a new record for points scored by a single team in any half of a bowl game. The previous record had been held by West Virginia, which scored 49 points in the first half of the 2012 Orange Bowl.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401032073 |title=Jarrett Stidham, Auburn throttle Purdue 63-14 at Music City Bowl |website=ESPN.com |date=December 27, 2018 |access-date=December 27, 2018}} ==Updated stadiums== *'''[[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]]''' completed its four-phase renovation of '''[[Mountain America Stadium|Sun Devil Stadium]]'''. The fourth and final phase includes reconstruction of the east sideline. The capacity is now 55,000, down from 71,706 just prior to the renovation.{{cite web|url=https://www.constructionequipmentguide.com/final-phase-of-construction-begins-at-sun-devil-stadium/40849|title=Final Phase of Construction Begins at Sun Devil Stadium|website=www.constructionequipmentguide.com|access-date=9 September 2018}} *'''[[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]]''' debuted its $160 million expansion of the north end zone of '''[[Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium]]'''. The expansion added 4,800 seats and new premium seating to the north end zone, boosting the capacity of the stadium to 80,800. *'''[[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]]''' debuted its $63 million new west end zone project at '''[[Sanford Stadium]]''', which relocates the locker room from the east side to the west side, as well as the addition of a new plaza and recruiting pavilion. The project increased the stadium's capacity by 500 seats. *'''[[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana]]''' debuted its $50 million south end zone complex at '''[[Memorial Stadium (Indiana)|Memorial Stadium]]'''. The project includes a new rehabilitation and treatment facility for athletes, additional academic and life skills support facilities, a multi-use outdoor terrace on the roof of the structure, and an entry plaza and green space at the south end of the stadium. A new 42 x 91.3 ft. video board was installed for the 2018 season in the completed south end zone. *'''[[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]]''' is currently rebuilding the north end zone of '''[[Kinnick Stadium]]'''. The $89.9 million upgrade will feature the addition of box seating, outdoor club seating and a new scoreboard. Some seating opened for the 2018 season, while the entire project is scheduled to be complete in 2019. * '''[[Liberty Flames football|Liberty]]''' completed an expansion of '''[[Williams Stadium]]''' during the 2018 season. The capacity was increased from 19,200 to 25,000 in time for the Flames' FBS debut, while construction on a new press box continued until midseason.{{cite news|url=https://www.wdbj7.com/content/news/Liberty-University-Stadium-groundskeeper-of-30-years-reflects-on-the-transformation-491856391.html |title=Liberty University stadium construction winding down, groundskeeper of 30 years reflects on the transformation |first=Siobhan |last=McGirl |publisher=[[WDBJ]] |location=[[Roanoke, Virginia|Roanoke, VA]] |date=August 27, 2018 |access-date=October 27, 2018}} *'''[[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]]''' debuted an expansion of the venue then known as '''[[L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium|Cardinal Stadium]]''', specifically the filling in of the north end zone. Two new video scoreboards were also installed. While Louisville had long publicized this expansion project as adding 10,000 seats, bringing the capacity to 65,000,{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2017/08/17/louisville-football-stunning-papa-johns-cardinal-stadium-expansion-still-pace-tom-jurich-says/577415001/|title='Stunning' Papa John's Cardinal Stadium expansion pace, Tom Jurich says|last=Jones|first=Steve|date=August 17, 2017|access-date=January 27, 2018|newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]]}} it acknowledged in February 2018 that the final capacity would instead be about 61,000.{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/05/23/how-many-seats-papa-johns-cardinal-stadium-expansion-include/633228002/|title=Papa John's Cardinal Stadium won't get as many new seats as you think|last=Lourim|first=Jake|date=May 23, 2018|access-date=July 18, 2018|newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]]}} ===Renamed stadiums=== '''[[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State]]''' announced on April 19, 2018, that an area financial institution, Public Service Credit Union, had paid $37.7 million over 15 years to place its name on the venue then known as Colorado State Stadium. The new stadium name was not revealed at that time because PSCU was in the process of changing its name, with the new name expected to be announced in June 2018. The deal did not affect the playing surface, which continues to be named after former Rams head coach [[Sonny Lubick]].{{cite news|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/football/2018/04/19/colorado-state-university-sells-naming-rights-campus-stadium-fort-collins/531368002/ |title=CSU's on-campus stadium naming rights sell for $37.7 million |first=Kelly |last=Lyell |newspaper=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan|Coloradoan]] |location=Fort Collins, CO |date=April 19, 2018 |access-date=April 25, 2018}} On June 5, the former PSCU announced its new name of Canvas Credit Union, with the CSU venue becoming '''[[Canvas Stadium]]'''.{{cite press release|url=http://csurams.com/news/2018/6/5/general-canvas-stadium-is-new-name-for-colorado-state-universitys-multipurpose-stadium.aspx |title=Canvas Stadium is new name for Colorado State University's multipurpose stadium |publisher=Colorado State Rams |date=June 5, 2018 |access-date=June 8, 2018}} '''[[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]]''' renamed their stadium to '''[[David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium]]''' in honor of alumnus [[David G. Booth|David Booth]] who donated $50 million to the school for renovations to the stadium.{{cite web |last1=Hancock |first1=Peter |title=KU football stadium to be renamed after donor David Booth|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2017/dec/20/ku-football-stadium-be-renamed-after-donor-david-b/|website=KU Sports|date=20 December 2017 |access-date=20 December 2017}} As noted above, '''Louisville''' removed the Papa John's name from '''Cardinal Stadium''' in the wake of the controversy over founder John Schnatter. ==Kickoff games== ==="Week Zero"=== The regular season began with four [[Week 0]] games on Saturday, August 25: * [[2018 UMass Minutemen football team|UMass]] defeated [[2018 Duquesne Dukes football team|Duquesne]], 63–15 * [[2018 Rice Owls football team|Rice]] defeated [[2018 Prairie View A&M Panthers football team|Prairie View A&M]], 31–28 *[[2018 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team|Hawaii]] defeated [[2018 Colorado State Rams football team|Colorado State]], 43–34, in the only in-conference matchup of the week * [[2018 Wyoming Cowboys football team|Wyoming]] defeated [[2018 New Mexico State Aggies football team|New Mexico State]], 29–7 ===Week 1=== The vast majority of FBS teams opened the season on Labor Day weekend.
